summary: Players roll dice each turn and use them as workers of varying strength to develop their province, buy goods, and gain karma, racing to make their money and fame markers cross on two tracks running in opposite directions. It's a tight, puzzly euro where dice-as-workers creates constant tactical decisions about which action is worth which die.
praised: Elegant win-condition (fame and money tracks crossing)
criticised: Some luck in dice rolls, though mitigated by karma points
Rules have a few fiddly exceptions

interaction.kind: shared market stalls and dice-draft turn order in a race to the finish
interaction.detail: Players affect each other mainly by depleting shared market goods or taking a favorable die/turn-order position before others can, and by racing along the money/fame tracks that end the game when they cross. Most of a turn is spent building your own province on your own board, with the shared elements functioning more as a common pool to watch than a space to fight over.
interaction.said: often described as a light, family-weight 'race' game with turn order and market tension rather than conflict

subsystems: province tile-building (temples, palaces, forts, mills → fame)
markets and goods trading (marketplace worker actions → money)
palace favor actions (Great Mogul, Raja Man Singh, terrace, etc. → direct fame/money/rerolls)
river boat progression (advancing the boat for money/fame bonuses and karma)
sources: fame from building tiles (2-4 fame depending on upgrade level)
money collected via market worker actions
palace action grants (e.g. Great Mogul: 2 fame; Raja Man Singh: 3 money)
river space rewards (money and/or fame, some multiplied by karma level)
fame/money track bonus spaces (extra workers, karma increases, boat advances)
scoring.how_you_win: You continuously push a fame marker clockwise and a money marker counter-clockwise around opposite tracks by developing your province, running markets, and using palace/river actions; the instant any player's two markers meet or cross, the round finishes and whichever qualifying player has pushed them furthest past each other wins.
scoring.score_note: race: win when fame/money markers meet
